//: TypeScript is being adopted incrementally, not all at once.
The bugs this codebase actually produced were not JavaScript being sloppy —
they were untyped BOUNDARIES: a state payload that grew a `duration` field
the API never sent, a `session.refresh` that did not exist, a `unit` prop
that reached one component and not the sibling next to it. Types on those
seams catch all three at build time.
So: allowJs keeps every existing .js/.jsx file compiling untouched, and
checkJs stays OFF so they are not retro-audited. New shared contracts are
written in .ts and the JS imports them normally. strict is on, because a
half-strict type is worse than none — it reads as a guarantee it is not.
